verdict_reason: Mechanical re-scoping of every test to organisation-filtered lookups is correct and the new 403 fulfilments test is sound, but the owner-stamp assertion hides under an unrelated title and the new requireTraderAccess gate has no test anywhere.

todos.issue: The create-path owner stamp (createNotification sets organisationId from the caller, AC 1) is asserted only as an extra line (177) inside saveNotification_shouldCreateNotificationWithGeneratedReferenceNumber, whose title claims only the generated reference number; no test title states that a new notification is stored with the caller's organisation as owner, and copyNotification tests (e.g. copyNotification_shouldRetainCopiedFields ~1912) assert nothing about the copy's organisationId.
todos.fix: Must: one test whose title states that a created notification stores the caller's organisation ID as its owner proves it, and the reference-number test asserts only what its title claims. One way: move the captor and line 177 into saveNotification_shouldStoreCallersOrganisationAsOwner_onCreate, and add the same assertion to a copy test titled for it (copyNotification_shouldOwnTheCopyByCallersOrganisation).

todos.issue: NotificationService.requireTraderAccess (new public method, NotificationService.java:441, called by DocumentController.java:93/123/174 to gate document endpoints by organisation) has no test here; DocumentControllerTest and DocumentControllerTrailingSlashTest stub it with doNothing(), and no IT exercises a document endpoint from another organisation, so removing its organisation check leaves every test green.
todos.fix: Must: a test fails if requireTraderAccess stops refusing a reference number that the caller's organisation does not own. One way: add requireTraderAccess_shouldThrowNotFound_whenReferenceNotOwnedByOrganisation stubbing findByReferenceNumberAndOrganisationId(ref, ORG_ID) to Optional.empty() and asserting NotFoundException containing the ref, plus a passing case for an owned ref.
